anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the USB-C receptacle J7's VBUS pin (A4) is wired to the red net label 'VBUS' (the power-mux output / pre-buck rail), not to '+5V'. On the Power sheet the TPS2121 mux U9 has OUT (pin 1) = VBUS and IN2 (pin 2) = +5V, so VBUS is the post-mux rail that can rise to ~12 V when the barrel jack is present.
anomalies.expected: The spec states the mux IN2 must be fed from the USB 'VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) → +5V net', and that 'this net [VBUS] is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux'. The USB-C VBUS pin should carry +5V (mux input), never the mux output VBUS.

evidence.quote: IN2 (pin 2) wired to USB +5V/VBUS, with a common OUT feeding the board's unregulated VBUS rail ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.

anomalies.impact: The USB-C VBUS pin is tied to the mux output instead of the mux input. With the 12 V barrel jack connected, the mux output (~12 V) appears on the USB-C VBUS pins, back-powering any attached host/device (potential damage), and the mux's seamless +5V/+12V arbitration is defeated because +5V is merged with VBUS; USB alone can no longer correctly power the board.

Reference designators are renumbered versus the spec but that is not itself an anomaly.
